module_title: The Foundations: Agriculture, Industry, and the 'Triple Disaster' (1st to 3rd)
introduction: The first three plans were the building blocks of a newly independent India. We see a shift from basic survival (food) to building massive industrial cathedrals.

core_concepts.title: First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)
core_concepts.description: Based on the 'Harrod-Domar Model'. The primary focus was on 'Agricultural Development' and irrigation. It was a massive success, achieving a growth rate of 3.6% against a target of 2.1%. Iconic dams like Bhakra-Nangal and Hirakud were started here.

core_concepts.title: Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)
core_concepts.description: Based on the 'P.C. Mahalanobis Model'. The focus shifted to 'Heavy Industries' and rapid industrialization. Giant Steel Plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established.

core_concepts.title: Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966)
core_concepts.description: Also known as the 'Gadgil Yojana'. Aimed for 'Self-reliance' in agriculture and industry. However, it was the 'Most Unsuccessful Plan' in Indian history (Target: 5.6%, Achieved: 2.8%) due to the Indo-China War (1962), Indo-Pak War (1965), and a severe drought.

core_concepts.title: Plan Holiday (1966-1969)
core_concepts.description: Due to the failure of the 3rd Plan and war-related exhaustion of resources, the government took a break from 5-year plans and implemented three 'Annual Plans'. The 'Green Revolution' was launched during this period.

important_entities.name: Foreign Aid for Steel Plants
important_entities.key_fact: A favorite for 'Match the Following' questions
important_entities.significance: 1. Bhilai (Chhattisgarh) -> Supported by USSR. 2. Durgapur (West Bengal) -> Supported by UK. 3. Rourkela (Odisha) -> Supported by West Germany.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often swap the models. Remember: 1st Plan = Harrod-Domar (H-D). 2nd Plan = Mahalanobis. Agriculture came before heavy machinery!

exam_strategy_tips: Direct Question: 'What was the duration of the Plan Holiday?' Answer: 1966 to 1969.
